issues.issue: [fixed 2026-10-28: receipts[3], detail[2] and detail[114] recategorized to Public Power District Sales Tax; review note kept on the statement line] This is the public power district 5% gross revenue (in-lieu) tax. It is split between General and Debt Service in the same ratio as the property tax levy (5,696/3,949 = 1.44; 115,339/79,812 = 1.45), which is how that tax is distributed. The user's rules put it in Public Power District Sales Tax (incl. 'NPPD 5%'), not other taxes. The same applies to detail[2] (5,696, p5) and detail[114] (3,949, p13).

[fixed 2026-10-28: User fees, Water hookups and Water late fees recategorized to Utility Charges] Utility fund user fees fall under the user's Utility Charges category (2026-10-28 rule: utility fund sales/charges/collections), not charges for services/fees. The same applies to receipts[26] Water hookups 850 and receipts[27] Water late fees 2,783.

[fixed 2026-10-28: recategorized to Employee Benefits and Payroll Taxes] Employee pension and insurance contributions are Employee Benefits and Payroll Taxes. The same label in the General Fund schedule (detail[29], p6) is employee benefits, so the report uses two categories for one label.
The user rule maps county treasurer balances to Cash and Cash Equivalents. As a 'due from' line this is defensible, but it doesn't match that rule.

[fixed 2026-10-28: receipts[18] and detail[17] recategorized to Utility Charges (detail refuse/sanitation charges)] Refuse/dumpsite receipts could be Utility Charges (incl. garbage/refuse) under the 2026-10-28 rule (also detail[17])
Recorded as printed in Other Financing Sources, but the Statement of Activities (p2) counts it as an operating grant for the library, so it's really grant revenue
